title: C. difficile infection (gut infection after antibiotics)

items: Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) is a bacterium that can cause diarrhoea and inflammation of the bowel.
It most often follows antibiotic use or a hospital stay.
Three or more loose or watery stools in 24 hours.
Belly pain and fever. Bloody stool is unusual with this infection.
A stool test for C. diff toxin or its genes. Your team may use two tests.
Blood tests including a blood count, kidney function, and albumin.
An X-ray or CT of the belly if the illness is severe.
Your doctor will choose treatment based on how severe the infection is.
Your doctor will decide about the antibiotic that may have caused it.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Wash hands with soap and water, especially after using the toilet.
Drink fluids to replace what you lose.
Tell your doctor if the diarrhoea returns after treatment.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Swollen, very painful belly, or no bowel movement with a swollen belly
Fainting, very low blood pressure, or confusion
